1. Core Clinical Tension: A 63-year-old man presenting with new-onset generalized tonic-clonic seizures, a subdural hemorrhage on CT brain, and unexplained bicytopenia (normocytic anemia and thrombocytopenia), with an incidental left lower lobe lung opacification. The core diagnostic tension is recognizing that the intracranial hemorrhage was precipitated by parasite-induced thrombocytopenia stemming from a giant calcified pulmonary hydatid cyst, despite negative echinococcal serology and absence of eosinophilia.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The presentation ends after initial emergency evaluation with GCS 14/15, baseline labs demonstrating bicytopenia, negative HIV/treponemal tests, CT brain showing right subdural hemorrhage with midline shift, and plain chest radiograph showing left lower lobe opacification, prior to inpatient internal medicine consultation, repeat thoracic CT, and serological assays.
3. Differential Distinctions: Differentiating hydatid lung disease from bronchogenic carcinoma or tuberculoma (broad differential for lung mass ruled out by pathognomonic cystic CT features), and distinguishing parasite-mediated bicytopenia from hematologic malignancy, drug-induced cytopenia, liver failure, or systemic autoimmune disease (ruled out by normal organ function and negative autoantibodies).
case_prompt: A 63-year-old man originally from the Eastern Cape province and residing in the Western Cape of South Africa presented to the emergency center with new-onset generalized tonic-clonic seizures. His medical history included hypertension, obesity, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. On physical examination, vital signs were normal; he had a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14/15 with no meningism, focal neurological deficits, petechiae, purpura, ecchymoses, lymphadenopathy, or hepatosplenomegaly. Initial complete blood count revealed bicytopenia with a hemoglobin of 8.0 g/dL and a platelet count of 54 × 10^9/L, with a normal total white cell count of 8.05 × 10^9/L and normal differential counts (eosinophils 0.15 × 10^9/L). Serum urea, creatinine, and electrolytes were normal. HIV ELISA and treponemal antibody screening tests were negative. Non-contrast computed tomography of the brain revealed an acute-on-chronic right subdural hemorrhage with a 4-mm midline shift and early right uncal herniation. A routine admission chest radiograph showed an opacification in the left lower lobe.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary Hematologic Malignancy / Autoimmune or Nutritional Cytopenia
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered to explain severe bicytopenia, but extensive evaluation showed no nutritional deficits, hemolysis, thyroid/hepatic dysfunction, or autoantibody markers.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Laboratory investigations revealed no evidence for nutritional deficiency, haemolysis, liver dysfunction and thyroid disease to account for the bicytopenia. An antinuclear antibody test and rheumatoid factor were also negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered on differential for a solitary pulmonary mass, but ruled out by typical, sharply defined cystic architecture with peripheral calcification on advanced computed tomography.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: While the differential for a lung mass is quite broad, given the typical CT findings, a presumptive diagnosis of hydatid disease was made.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Cross-sectional thoracic CT demonstrating a massive, calcified cystic lesion in the lung, followed by hematologic recovery upon antihelminthic therapy, established the diagnosis despite negative serum ELISA.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest and abdomen (Figure 3) showed a cystic lesion with enhancing capsule due to calcifications in the left lower lobe measuring 91 mm anteroposterior x 90 mm transverse.

editor_comments: Distilled admission teaching case for pulmonary Echinococcosis presenting with bicytopenia and subdural hematoma. Admission breakpoint captures initial emergency neuro/triage findings. Zero pathogen spoilers. Verbatim quotes verified.
